kept: one direct child in its own session and process group
bounded capture, deadlines, no retry, receipts, handles closed
a live member of the child's process group after exit refuses the run
SIGTERM then SIGKILL of the group within 2,000 ms
not_kept: orphaned descendants re-parented to the supervisor (Darwin re-parents them to launchd)
guarantees.source_backed_property: the probe, module loader and 24 reader files contain no process-creation call (reviewed static check MC11)

assertion_meanings.reaped: the direct child was reaped; orphaned descendants are re-parented to launchd, not to the supervisor
assertion_meanings.process_group_absent: killpg(pid, 0) finds no member of the child's group; whether Darwin counts a zombie member is not established
assertion_meanings.cleanup.passed: the group was gone within the cleanup ceiling, with the two meanings above

supervisor.durability: the probe's fs.fsyncSync is unchanged; on macOS fsync does not force data to permanent storage as F_FULLFSYNC does; results claim no durability beyond fsync

preparer.publication: renamex_np(staged, destination, RENAME_EXCL) from libSystem within one volume; ENOTSUP or any failure refuses; never a fallback rename
preparer.flag_binding: the implementation binds RENAME_EXCL's value from the SDK header or Apple's documentation and proves no-replace with control MC15

fields: product version, build, ProductVersionExtra, and the OS cryptex's SystemVersion.plist if present
Git implementation used for source reads: absolute path (not the /usr/bin/git dispatcher), SHA-256, version from one bounded --version start
M0.launcher: -I -S -B; package metadata read by explicit path under the venv's site-packages, not through importlib.metadata

M1.optional: one codesign --verify --strict inspection start, counted separately; not required

host_observation.closure_claim: The Node executable's bytes and load commands and the interpreter files of section 4 are bound; the system libraries come from the OS build's dyld shared cache in the signed system volume and the OS cryptex and are identified only by the recorded OS product version, build and cryptex version, not by per-file hashes; Apple's sealed system volume and SIP are assumed, not verified.
canonical_paths: every bound path recorded canonically (realpath once, rechecked before use)
/tmp, /var and /etc resolve into /private; any other symlinked ancestor refuses
qualifying runs use a resolved temporary directory
a .DS_Store or other untracked file in a source, evidence or dependency tree refuses it
host_observation.boot_binding: the provider reads kern.bootsessionuuid before the cohort and before and after each start; a change fails the attempt; the probe checks os.type(), os.release(), os.machine() and the OS build file, and no longer checks the boot itself (stated weakening of E19)
host_observation.N34_M: before a macOS execution plan is adopted, an independent reviewer examines the Mach-O parser's source and the closure claim against the actual load commands; an external review obligation, not a runtime pass
host_observation.execution_plan_rules: P07 section 2 (E9, E17): literal argv with cwd, environment and limits; canonical paths; no TODO, null, wildcard, guessed hash or unresolved field; existing external evidence parent with ancestor identities; absent per-attempt output paths; approved failure capture; independent review with an externally supplied digest

selection_rule.qualifying_run: driver receives --readback-config and --readback-config-sha256 from an independently reviewed execution plan; all existing rules apply; any skip, error, expected failure or missing method of the readback cohort fails the run; only a qualifying run can be cited for the readback methods, the macOS qualification or R03
selection_rule.ordinary_run: neither argument: the driver proceeds with every stage, records readback_selection {status: absent, run_kind: ordinary} and passes no selection to the unit process; the readback CPU class's setUpClass fails visibly with 'No approved current-host readback selection: ordinary run, not a qualification' (setup error, never a skip); coordinator seams run; the unit stage is failed for this reason under both drivers' rule that any skip, error or failure fails a stage; no ordinary run is evidence for the readback methods
selection_rule.partial_selection: fails in either kind of run
selection_rule.direct_invocation: without the driver: an ordinary run (visible setup error) unless both selection variables are set, as P05 section 2 provides
selection_rule.amends: only the driver's refusal to start without a selection, for ordinary runs; P05's no-skip rule and CH13's 'fails visibly; no skip' stay
rejected_alternatives: revision 1's labelled skip for ordinary runs: adds a skip, which P05 forbids, and changes no stage outcome under the drivers' zero-skip rule
requiring a selection for every run: main's ordinary routine would run no stage without one
selection_rule.r04_consequence: in main's ordinary runs the three CPU methods change from skipped to visible setup errors; R04 records this under OK-ENG-009 section 4 as the unchanged outcome of an explicitly incomplete feature, with exact inputs
